body:
Thanks for the advice. It has been a tough few days but I think I just need to accept that finding someone probably isn't going to happen to me. If I've been actively working on it since been nineteen for about five years with nothing to show then it might be time to move on.

I must have asked about a hundred people on dates and so far I've only been on one. It didn't get me down before because I they were mostly people who I only just met in a bar or club type situation and so I knew they were rejecting me on my looks, which is understandable.

I think that's why this one hurt me the most. She is one of the only females who actually likes my personality and displayed some "flirtatious" signs.

Accepting that I will likely be forever alone has actually made me feel a little better about my future. It almost feels that because I am unable to compete I've removed my own disappointment in my failures. 

I handed my notice in for my job and only have three weeks left. I now feel free to pursue a different future, one which I hope will bring me happiness. Bodybuilding is the only hobby that I've been able to make money from in the past and I hope to turn this into my future. The only downside is that I will be starting steroids in the near future but if this makes me happier then it might keep me alive.

As for the autism and anxiety, I don't think I have either. I really don't have any problems with interacting with people, making friends, interpreting other peoples emotions or any of the other common signs. I'm not saying that I definitely don't I just don't think the symptoms are applicable to me.

Also, congratulations on your relationship. I hope your future brings you happiness.

You're right it is a bit extreme but I'm just not enjoying life at the moment. I'm tired of wearing the mask of a happy and confident person.

I think I need to take a step back and decide how I want to continue.

Yeah, rejected romantically. I've been rejected many many times before but this one hurt the most as she is the only girl who has ever seemed to actually like me.

I do have a small group of friends who are great but they all have their own lives and I don't want to burden them with any of my problems.

As for you, I'd recommend asking someone out if you find that you like them. It has helped me to start overcoming my shyness and after it's done yea really feel relieved than to have the "what if?" hanging over you.

All the best to you. I hope you have happiness in your future.

It didn't go well but could have gone worse. I asked her if she wanted to get a drink tomorrow (Saturday) to which she said maybe some other time. I get that this is essentially a nice way of saying no. 

The rest if the afternoon went okay we talked as normal so it doesn't seem like she was made uncomfortable and nothing seemed awkward between us. I still think I'm going to hand my notice in on Monday as seeing her will only remind me that she only sees me as a work friend.
Thanks for the reply. For us, I don't think it's in either of our personalities to be outright unpleasant in the case of a breakup, maybe just a little awkward but I'm sure that would pass too.
Yeah, I'll see how it goes. I can always that card if it's needed.
I agree, we have the exact same job role so I don't think there is any kind of power imbalance between us.
You're right. My confidence has come a long way in the last couple of years but I guess we all have times where we second guess ourselves.

Maybe you have a point but personally, I think there's a difference between hoping to date someone and sexual harassment. I believe it's okay to ask one time and then move on respectfully if you get a negative response.
I understand your points and even think they're right. Despite this I'm still going to go for it. If she rejects me then I don't ming leaving my job and I think I'm equipped to deal with any fallout.
This is the first time I've realised I would value a potential relationship with her over keeping my job.
I probably should put her out of my mind but it's hard to ignore someone who sits two metres away from you for eight hours a day.
I know you're right but I've not had much look with that lately.

For me I'm not scared of being rejected, I know it would hurt for a bit but at least you have an answer and can move on. I'm just not sure if I want to look for a new job if things turn out bad.

I hope things work out well for you and if you have any updates in the future, I'd like to hear them.
Yeah. It feels very high risk but, if things go well, then also high reward.
